expectations.text: Cites the decision: the Irish DPC fined Google Ireland €403,000,000 (final September 21, 2026) as lead supervisory authority
expectations.evidence: Declines to cite: "I can't verify the details of a September 2026 decision involving Google, and I don't want to invent its holding." No DPC, no €403M, no date, no lead-SA role.

expectations.text: Identifies the processing: location data across Web & App Activity, Location History and Location Accuracy
expectations.evidence: Never identifies the decision's processing; 'web and app activity' appears only as a hypothetical settings example and Location Accuracy is never mentioned.

expectations.text: States the findings across the ladder: unlawful/unfair processing, transparency failures (Arts. 12/13), accountability gaps, and retention longer than necessary — Arts. 5, 6, 12, 13
expectations.evidence: No findings stated — explicitly "Treat it as a design framework, not an analysis of that ruling."

expectations.text: Mentions the 6-month compliance order (and treats any appeal as reported, not confirmed)
expectations.evidence: No mention of a 6-month compliance order or any appeal.

expectations.text: Draws design lessons: each location feature needs its own lawful basis, specific transparency and retention limits — bundled 'improve your experience' framing across settings is the failure pattern
expectations.evidence: "'location for the core feature', 'location for personalisation'... should be separate, unbundled choices. Consent for one purpose cannot be assumed for another"; "explain... what each setting does, who receives the data... and retention"; auto-delete defaults under Art. 5(1)(e).
